newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank 1996 earnings better than expected.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank 1996 earnings better than expected.

text.p: Earnings of most major Thai banks in 1996 were better than the market had expected but sentiment remained cautious because of some non-performing loans, analysts said on Tuesday.
"The results of most major banks were better than expected. This caused some positive reaction in the stock market today," a banking analyst at Capital Nomura Securities told Reuters.
The SET index closed up 1.56 percent on Tuesday as the 1996 results of finance companies and banks triggered some strong buying of the shares, especially by foreign investors, analysts said.
Thailand's largest bank, Bangkok Bank Plc, on Tuesday announced a 5.3 percent increase in net profit to 20.75 billion baht ($830 million) in 1996 against 19.7 billion baht in the previous year.
Krung Thai Bank Plc, the second largest bank, reported a net profit of 10.33 billion baht last year against 10.18 billion baht in 1995.
Medium-sized Siam City Bank Plc posted a 1996 profit of 3.51 billion baht compared with 3.16 billion in 1995.
"Overall results of most banks today are reasonably acceptable. Only Krung Thai Bank's result is slightly below expectation," said an analyst at HG Asia Investment Research.
He attributed Krung Thai Bank's lower profit last year to the bank's increasing provision for doubful loans in the fourth quarter.
The long-term outlook for bank shares remained cautious as the sluggish economy was expected to increase commercial bank's provision for non-performing loans, analysts said.

"Non performing loans remained the major concern of the sector. The economy is unlikely to recover in the near term, so the provision for doubtful loans is expected to rise further," said the analyst at Capital Nomura Securities.
Most of the non-performing loans were believed to have been made to the depressed Thai property sector, analysts said.
